newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS sugar output down 3.16 pct - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar output down 3.16 pct - DataNet.

text.p: Brazilian center-south sugar output by June 16 totalled 1.74 million tonnes, down 3.16 percent on the 1.80 million tonnes produced to the same stage last year, said independent consultants DataNet-Agricommodities.
Sugarcane crushings were marginally down on 1996/97, reaching 47.19 million tonnes to June 16, 0.16 percent lower than the 47.27 million tonnes seen last year, it added.

The slower crushings and the fall in sugar production DataNet attributed to a series of cold fronts which brought heavy, unseasonal rains to the main growing regions throughout the two-week period to June 16.
The rainfall contributed to a reduction in the sugar content which was on average one percent below that during the same stage last year.
Up to June 1, sugarcane and sugar output had been running 19.12 percent and 32.26 percent ahead of last year respectively.
Alcohol production was still well ahead of last year, totaling 2.58 million cubic meters, up 11.01 percent on the 2.32 million cubic meters produced to the same stage in 1996/97.
However the growth rate has slowed down from the previous two-week period, when alcohol output was running 30.08 percent ahead of 1996/97.

Unica, which has replaced the Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries of Sao Paulo (AIAA), traditionally begins monitoring crop production from May 1. The trend is still for a greater percentage of hydrous alcohol over anhydrous than in the previous year, DataNet said.
Hydrous alcohol represented around 73 percent of total alcohol production in the two weeks to June 16 as opposed to 68 percent in the corresponding period last year.
Total alcohol stocks in the center-south are estimated at 1.64 million cubic meters (76 percent hydrous and 24 percent anhydrous alcohol), up 83 percent on stock levels at the same stage in 1996/97.

During the two-week period, 34 percent of sugar output was shipped abroad, an increase of six percent on the same period last year. This combined with the drop in production helped support domestic prices.
Crystal sugar prices, which in the last week of May this year were 23.74 percent down on last year's levels, were only 20.18 percent lower in the final week in June, DataNet said.
Sugar stocks were around 7.66 percent down on the same stage last year, it added.
The two-week period to July 1 is expected to show an increase in sugar content because of drier weather.
But other factors apart from weather are holding back the harvest in some regions, DataNet said.

In the region around Catanduva which represents around 10 percent of Sao Paulo output and eight percent of total center-south production, the banning of cane burning for environmental reasons is causing considerable crushing delays.
